Annual Report

Acme Industries — 2025

Financial highlights, operations review, and outlook for FY2026
Prepared by: Office of the CFO  ·  Document ID: AR-2025-0317  ·  March 2026

1. Executive Summary

FY2025 was a year of disciplined growth for Acme Industries. Consolidated revenue reached $418.2M, an increase of 14.7% over the prior year, driven by sustained momentum in our Industrial Automation segment and the successful integration of the Boreal acquisition completed in Q2.

Operating margin expanded by 180 basis points to 19.4%, reflecting both pricing discipline and the realization of synergies from prior-year restructuring. We exited the year with $112M in cash and equivalents and zero net debt.

"Our results in 2025 demonstrate that focused execution, even in a softer macroeconomic environment, produces durable value." — M. Tanaka, Chief Executive Officer

2.2 Profitability

Gross margin improved to 41.2% (from 39.8%) as a result of favorable input cost trends and a more profitable product mix. SG&A as a percentage of revenue declined to 17.8%, reaching the long-term target communicated to shareholders in 2023.

3. Operations Review

The Springfield and Lyon facilities completed Phase II of their automation upgrade program in October. Combined unit output capacity has increased by 22% with no incremental headcount, supporting our committed 2026 delivery schedule for the new APEX-7 platform.

3.1 Safety and quality

  • Total Recordable Incident Rate: 0.41, lowest in company history
  • First-pass yield: 98.3% across all production lines
  • Customer return rate: 0.18%, down from 0.24% in FY2024

3.2 Sustainability

Scope 1 and 2 emissions decreased by 11.4% on an absolute basis. We remain on track to meet our 2030 commitment of a 50% reduction relative to the 2020 baseline.

4. Outlook

For FY2026, the board has approved a capital plan of $34M, weighted toward digital products and capacity expansion at the Lyon facility. Management guidance calls for revenue between $455M and $475M, with operating margin in the 19.5–20.5% range.

We continue to evaluate selective M&A opportunities, with a clear preference for software-enabled hardware businesses that complement the Industrial Automation portfolio.

5. Closing remarks

We thank our 2,140 employees for another year of exceptional commitment, and our shareholders for their continued confidence. Acme is built to compound value over decades, not quarters, and 2025 was another step on that long journey.
